citations.title: Staff Member and Service Provider Requirements – program manager
citations.requirement: Program provider must employ or contract with a person who oversees HCS/CFC services. That person needs 3 years of verified experience: paid work, agency-verified, or microboard.

citations.title: Staff Member and Service Provider Requirements – direct service qualifications
citations.requirement: Staff of supervised living, residential support, respite, etc. must meet HCS Billing Requirements/Appendix C criteria. They need individual-specific training before service and every 12 months, plus observed competency.

citations.title: Person Centered Planning course
citations.requirement: A service provider or staff member who helps develop an implementation plan for CFC PAS/HAB must complete the HHSC-approved Online Introductory Course to Person Centered Planning within 90 days of hire.

citations.title: Qualified providers of nursing, dental and professional therapies
citations.requirement: Policy ensuring only qualified, licensed providers in good standing and within scope of license serve. Behavioral support providers take HHSC web training before service, within 90 days of revision, and every 3 years.

citations.title: CFC PAS/HAB service provider qualifications
citations.requirement: CFC PAS/HAB providers: at least 18, diploma or documented proficiency evaluation with 3 references, not the individual's spouse or a minor's parent. Individual or LAR may train the provider on request.

citations.title: Program Provider Requirements – continuous availability
citations.requirement: Program provider must ensure continuous availability of trained, qualified service providers to deliver required services, based on each individual's needs and characteristics.

citations.title: Program Provider Requirements – criminal history and background checks
citations.requirement: Comply with 40 TAC §49.304 and §49.312. Obtain DPS criminal history before hire. Do not hire anyone with a Health & Safety Code §250.006 offense, a registered sex offender, or an offense the provider deems a contraindication.

citations.title: Program Provider Requirements – registry and exclusion searches
citations.requirement: Search Employee Misconduct Registry and Nurse Aide Registry before hire and every 12 months. Search HHS-OIG and HHSC-OIG exclusion lists before hire and monthly. Do not employ listed persons.

citations.title: Program Provider Requirements – transportation policy
citations.requirement: Develop and implement policy ensuring only staff and service providers with a valid driver's license and insurance transport individuals. Revise the policy if a shortcoming is identified.

citations.title: Program Provider Requirements – individual's choice of service provider
citations.requirement: Employ or contract with the person or entity chosen by the individual or LAR if qualified and willing. Otherwise document good cause for not doing so.

citations.title: Program Provider Requirements – conflict of interest, financial impropriety, abuse/neglect/exploitation policy
citations.requirement: Written policy preventing conflicts of interest, financial impropriety, abuse/neglect/exploitation, damage to or blocked access to possessions, and threats of these. Only room and board payment is exempt from the goods-and-services rule.

citations.title: Program Provider Requirements – advance directives
citations.requirement: Program provider must comply with 42 U.S.C. §1396a(w) requirements about advance directives.

citations.title: Nursing – scope and delivery
citations.requirement: Nursing must follow the PDP, IPC, implementation plan, Nursing Practice Act, 22 TAC Ch. 217, 224, 225 and waiver Appendix C. Includes medication administration, health monitoring, emergency referrals, delegation and teaching.

citations.title: Nursing – RN assessment, documentation and delegation
citations.requirement: RN performs and documents a nursing assessment before unlicensed staff perform any nursing task and when health needs change. RN develops the nursing portion of the implementation plan and documents delegation decisions.

citations.title: Nursing – unlicensed medication administration (Hum. Res. Code Ch. 161)
citations.requirement: Unlicensed staff may give oral, topical or metered-dose inhaler medications for stable, predictable conditions after RN assessment and RN/LVN training or competency check. RN/LVN reviews at least annually and after significant change.

citations.title: Nursing – screening tool and refusal of nursing assessment
citations.requirement: The Nursing Task Screening Tool may show no assessment is needed. If an individual or LAR refuses an assessment, limit services as specified, immediately notify the individual or LAR and service coordinator in writing, and send the notice to HHSC.

citations.title: Residential Requirements – home condition and safety
citations.requirement: Applies to three- and four-person residences. Home must be clean, pest-free and accessible, with working appliances and HVAC. Mattresses off the floor, chemicals secured, perishables stored safely, pets vaccinated, and adaptive equipment functional or documented.

citations.title: Residential Requirements – hot water temperature and skills assessment
citations.requirement: Hot water at sinks and bathing facilities must not exceed 120°F unless a face-to-face competency-based skills assessment shows every resident can regulate temperature. Repeat annually, document, and keep a copy in the residence.

citations.title: Residential Requirements – means of escape, smoke alarms, extinguishers
citations.requirement: Unobstructed exterior doors; two means of escape from the home and from each bedroom (one if sprinklered and maintained). Working smoke alarms in and outside bedrooms; extinguishers on each level, serviced after use.

citations.title: Residential Requirements – fire drills
citations.requirement: Per residence: a drill at least every 90 days and four per 365 days, two during sleeping hours. Each staff member drills within 90 days of hire and annually, with retraining and plan revision as needed.

citations.title: Residential Requirements – emergency plans
citations.requirement: Staff review each resident's emergency plans before serving. Residence keeps plans for location-relevant emergencies, individual needs and fire drill responses, and posts emergency numbers where staff can easily see them.

citations.title: Residential Requirements – infection control
citations.requirement: Use standard precautions and hand hygiene. Written policies for preventing and controlling communicable disease among employees and individuals, including transmission-based precautions and protective measures when an employee contracts a disease.

citations.title: Residential Requirements – medication administration and storage
citations.requirement: Written policies to prevent unauthorized access to medications. Safe administration procedure, staff knowledgeable about each resident's medications, and staff RN-trained and delegated. Accurate, accessible administration documentation.

citations.title: Residential Requirements – four-person residence
citations.requirement: Before providing RSS: local or State Fire Marshal inspection with cited items corrected, plus HHSC approval. Renew certification annually, keep the latest inspection in the home, and stay in continuous compliance with codes and laws. HHSC Forms 5604/5606 apply only if inspectors refuse.

citations.title: Finances and Rent – room and board charges
citations.requirement: Collect room (rent or allowed ownership costs plus listed shared items and utilities) and board (food and cooking supplies) only as itemized. Use an equitable formula, never exceed the formula amount, and document it. No increase when a resident moves out.

citations.title: Finances and Rent – residential agreement
citations.requirement: Before an individual or LAR selects a residence, the provider must have a written residential agreement with the individual or LAR.

citations.title: Finances and Rent – other charges against personal funds
citations.requirement: Other charges must be reasonable and comparable to community cost. Explain each charge and its effect on finances. Get written agreement before assessing. Never charge for items or services reimbursed by HCS or CFC.

citations.title: Finances and Rent – management of personal funds
citations.requirement: On written request, manage funds free of charge. No commingling; separate detailed record of deposits and expenditures; process showing the individual acknowledged spending money. Accrued expenses need a written payment plan.

citations.title: HHSC Surveys of a Program Provider – survey types and certification period
citations.requirement: Continuous compliance required. Unannounced initial, recertification, follow-up, residential and intermittent surveys. Initial survey within 120 calendar days after first enrollment or transfer approval; certification lasts no more than 365 days.

citations.title: HHSC Surveys of a Program Provider – residential visits
citations.requirement: HHSC makes an unannounced visit to each SL/RSS residence at least annually. It may require corrective action or a written safety plan before the visit ends, evidence of correction, or an intermittent survey.

citations.title: HHSC Surveys of a Program Provider – exit conference, amelioration and corrective action
citations.requirement: HHSC reviews services to any individual and checks implementation of an approved amelioration plan (§565.47). Exit conference gives written preliminary findings, including possible critical violations. Action follows §565.49.

citations.title: HHSC Approval of Four Person Residences
citations.requirement: Before RSS in a four-person residence, submit address/county, RSS-intent certification, fire-safety certification and certification that only permitted persons live there. HHSC responds in writing within 14 calendar days.

citations.title: Requirements for Program Provider Owned or Controlled Residential Settings
citations.requirement: Bedroom privacy, option of no roommate and choice of roommate, lock at no cost to the individual, and decorating freedom. Freedom to control unplanned schedule, food at any time, visitors at any time, accessible and hazard-free home.

citations.title: Modification of settings requirements by PDP
citations.requirement: A modification to a (b)(1)-(7) right needs a specific assessed need. Notify the service coordinator, who convenes the planning team to update the PDP. The provider implements only after the PDP is updated.

citations.title: Requirements for Home and Community-Based Service Settings
citations.requirement: General HCBS service-setting requirements that §263.502 builds on. Title confirmed by cross-reference; section text not fetched, so read it before drafting.

citations.title: Certification Standards: Individual's Rights
citations.requirement: Subchapter confirmed in the chapter table of contents as the certification standard for individual's rights. Section text not fetched, so pull §565.5 for the rights wording.

citations.title: Emergency Response System
citations.requirement: Subchapter confirmed in the chapter table of contents. Section text not fetched, so confirm applicability before drafting.

citations.cite: 26 TAC Chapter 565, Subchapter E (§§565.11–565.21) and Subchapter F (§§565.23–565.39)
citations.title: Certification Standards: Service Delivery; Quality Assurance
citations.requirement: Table of contents confirms these section ranges. Sections 565.13, 565.23 and 565.27 are verified above; other sections in these ranges still need their text pulled before citing.

citations.title: LIDDA Requirements for Providing Service Coordination in the HCS Program
citations.requirement: Cross-referenced by §565.13(e) and §263.502 for the service coordinator's role (refused nursing assessment, PDP modifications). Text not fetched.

citations.title: Definitions (three-person and four-person residence, program provider, LIDDA, LON)
citations.requirement: Three-person residence houses 1–3 individuals; four-person residence houses 1–4, and with four residents at least one receives RSS. Provider leases or owns the home; only staff and spouses may live there besides residents.

citations.title: Description of HCS Program Services
citations.requirement: RSS staff must be present and awake whenever an individual is present. SL staff must be present and able to respond during sleeping hours. There is no numeric ratio.

citations.title: LON Assignment
citations.requirement: Level of need (LON 1, 5, 8, 6, 9) is assigned from ICAP service levels and documentation. LON 9 requires dedicated staff at least 16 waking hours a day. Provider enters the ID/RC assessment before it expires.

citations.title: Program Provider Reimbursement
citations.requirement: No payment without an authorized IPC, current ID/RC assessment and LOC determination. No payment while the individual is an inpatient in a hospital, nursing facility or ICF. Claims follow §52.121.

citations.title: HCS Interest List
citations.requirement: LIDDAs maintain the HCS interest list, served first-come first-served. Providers receive enrollees through the LIDDA choice list.

citations.title: Process for Individual to Transfer to a Different Program Provider or FMSA
citations.requirement: Defines how an individual transfers to a different program provider. Use it for transfer-out and transition-planning procedures.

citations.title: HCBS settings requirements (1915(c) waivers)
citations.requirement: Federal HCBS settings standards for provider-owned or controlled residences: person-centered plan, rights, privacy, choice, access to community. Any modification must be supported by assessed need and documented.

citations.title: Personal Care Services that Require the Use of EVV
citations.requirement: EVV applies to CFC PAS/HAB, in-home respite and in-home ISS in the individual's own or family home. SL/RSS in 3- and 4-person provider homes are outside own-home EVV.

citations.title: Community Homes for Disabled Persons Location Act
citations.requirement: A community home holds no more than 6 residents plus 2 supervisors. Community homes must be spaced half a mile apart. Confirm local application before opening a home.

citations.title: Provisional Contract
citations.requirement: Every new contractor, and every existing contractor entering a new service area, starts with a provisional contract.

citations.title: Provisional Contract Application Process
citations.requirement: HHSC gives one opportunity to correct a deficient application, due within 30 days. Packet includes DPS criminal history acknowledgments for each controlling person.

citations.title: Additional Provisional Contract Application Requirements (HCS)
citations.requirement: HCS applicants complete provider applicant training and pass the competency exam with at least 85%. Exempt if holding a standard HCS contract in another service area.

citations.title: License, Certification, Accreditation, and Other Requirements
citations.requirement: Lists no facility license for HCS. Pathway is an HHSC contract and Ch. 565 certification, not an assisted living (Ch. 553) or HCSSA license.

citations.title: Provisional Contract Application Approval
citations.requirement: On approval, the contract is placed on the choice list for the program and area. A provisional contract may be extended once for up to 1 year.

citations.title: Standard Contract
citations.requirement: HHSC may offer a standard contract during the provisional term. Provider must respond per HHSC instructions or face an application denial period.

citations.title: Contractor requirement to subscribe to HHSC GovDelivery
citations.requirement: Contractors must subscribe to HHSC GovDelivery for information letters and provider alerts. Rate and policy changes are announced this way.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Program Manager Responsibilities
state_specifics: The HCS program provider is a contractor with HHSC. It holds no facility license (not an assisted living or HCSSA license).
Employ or contract with a program manager who oversees HCS services. The manager needs 3 years of verified paid, agency-verified or microboard experience (§565.7(a)).
Ensure continuous availability of trained, qualified service providers based on each individual's needs (§565.9(a)).
Governing authority resolution (Form 2031) names who may sign for the entity.

policies.title: HHSC Contract, Certification and Provider Agreements
state_specifics: Pathway: TMHP enrollment, then provider applicant training (PAT, 85% or higher on the exam), then a provisional contract through the CAMP portal.
One chance to correct a deficient application, due within 30 days of the suspense letter.
On approval the contract is placed on the choice list. A provisional contract can be extended once, for up to 1 year.
Respond to any HHSC standard-contract offer per HHSC instructions to avoid an application denial period.
Service area: serve every county in each area chosen on Form 3691-A.

policies.title: Policy Review, Document Control and HHSC Notifications
state_specifics: Designate a staff member who subscribes to HHSC GovDelivery (§52.103(g)). Log each information letter and provider alert, and the policy changes it triggers.
Revise a policy whenever HHSC or a survey identifies a shortcoming (e.g., transportation policy, §565.9(c)).
Review all policies at least annually and after any rule or rate change, and keep version history.

policies.title: Quality Improvement, Data Review and Mortality Review
state_specifics: Review trends quarterly: incidents, medication errors, drill results, grievances, restraint use and hospitalizations.
Review every death, using the Death of an Individual policy (HW-06).
Track survey findings and amelioration or corrective-action plans to completion.
Quality-review the HCBS settings protections in each home at least annually.

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing and Service Documentation
state_specifics: Bill only with an authorized IPC, a current ID/RC assessment and an LOC determination (§263.601).
Do not bill days an individual is an inpatient in a hospital, nursing facility or ICF.
SL and RSS in 3- and 4-person provider homes are not own-home EVV services (1 TAC §354.4005). Separately track any EVV-required services, such as in-home respite and CFC PAS/HAB in own/family homes.
Claims and IPC revisions go through the TMHP LTC Online Portal. Cost reports go through STEPS.
Per diem unit: 1 day = 18 hours, billed at the correct LON and service code.

policies.title: Conflict of Interest and Financial Impropriety
state_specifics: Written policy preventing conflicts of interest and financial impropriety (§565.9(g)).
Staff and the provider may not exchange goods or services with individuals. Only the room and board payment is exempt.
Prohibit damaging, or blocking access to, an individual's possessions, and threats of those acts.
Staff disclose conflicts to the program manager in writing.

policies.title: HHSC Survey Readiness, Exit Conference and Corrective Action
state_specifics: Initial certification survey is unannounced, within 120 calendar days of HHSC approving the first individual's enrollment or transfer.
Certification lasts no more than 365 days, with unannounced recertification surveys.
HHSC makes an unannounced visit to each SL/RSS home at least annually. It may require on-the-spot correction or a written safety plan.
Exit conference gives written preliminary findings, including possible critical violations. Submit the amelioration plan per §565.47 and track the follow-up under §565.49.
Keep survey-ready binders in each home: drills, emergency plans, RN assessments, hot-water skills assessments, rights and finance records.

policies.title: Level of Need, ID/RC Assessment and IPC Maintenance
state_specifics: LON (1, 5, 8, 6, 9) is assigned from ICAP service levels and documentation (§263.106).
Enter the ID/RC assessment in the HHSC system before it expires.
LON 9 requires a staff member dedicated to that individual for at least 16 waking hours a day.
Document dangerous-behavior or medical-need changes that support an LON or IPC revision.

policies.title: Community Home Location and Local Land-Use Compliance
state_specifics: Hum. Res. Code Ch. 123: a community home holds no more than 6 residents plus 2 supervisors, with half-mile spacing between community homes. Confirm local application before opening a home.
Three-person residence: 1–3 individuals. Four-person residence: 1–4, with at least one receiving RSS when four live there.
The program provider leases or owns the home. Only staff and their spouses may live there besides residents.

policies.title: Individual Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
state_specifics: Bedroom privacy, with the option of no roommate and a choice of roommate.
Bedroom lock at no cost to the individual. Keys held only by the individual, roommate and designated staff.
Freedom to decorate and to control unplanned schedules, with food at any time and visitors at any time.
Home must be accessible and hazard-free.

policies.title: Rights Modifications and Due Process
state_specifics: A modification of any §263.502(b)(1)-(7) right requires a specific assessed need.
Notify the service coordinator, who convenes the planning team to update the PDP.
Implement the modification only after the PDP is updated. Review it periodically and document it.
Provide the individual and LAR with written notice and a way to object.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Give each individual and LAR the grievance process and external complaint contacts at admission and annually.
No retaliation for a complaint. Complaints about abuse, neglect or exploitation follow BP-03.
Record each grievance, the response and the resolution date.
Add the HHSC and IDD Ombudsman contact details after confirming them with HHSC before publication.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Designate a privacy officer and train all staff at hire.
Release records only with consent from the individual or LAR, or as law permits.
Protect electronic records, texts and photos.
Notify affected parties of any breach per 45 CFR 164 Subpart D.

policies.title: Personal Funds and Property Management
state_specifics: Manage funds only on written request, and free of charge (§565.27(e)).
No commingling. Keep a separate detailed record of deposits and expenditures.
Keep a process showing the individual acknowledged each spending-money disbursement.
Accrued expenses need a written payment plan.
Maintain a property inventory. Never charge for items or services reimbursed by HCS or CFC.

policies.title: Room and Board Charges and Residential Agreement
state_specifics: Written residential agreement must be in place before the individual or LAR selects the residence (§565.27(a)(6)).
Charge only itemized room (rent or allowed ownership cost, shared items, utilities) and board (food, cooking supplies), divided by an equitable formula.
Never exceed the formula amount. Document the calculation. No increase to remaining residents when someone moves out.
Other charges must be reasonable and comparable to community cost. Explain each charge and its financial effect, and get written agreement before assessing.

policies.title: Informed Consent and Decision-Making Support
state_specifics: Identify whether the individual has a legally authorized representative (LAR) and document the authority.
Support the individual to make their own choices, with accessible information.

When an individual or LAR refuses a nursing assessment, limit services as specified, notify the individual/LAR and service coordinator in writing immediately, and send the notice to HHSC (§565.13(b)-(e)).

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
state_specifics: Provide interpreters, translated materials and communication supports at no cost.
Give information in the individual's preferred language and format.
Accessible home and equipment. Document and maintain adaptive equipment (§565.23(b)).

policies.title: Advance Directives
state_specifics: Provide written information on advance directive rights at admission, as 42 USC 1396a(w) requires.
Do not condition care on whether an advance directive exists. Document the individual's wishes.
Make staff aware of each individual's directives and where they are kept.

policies.title: Individual's Choice of Service Providers
state_specifics: Employ or contract with the person or entity the individual or LAR chooses, if that person is qualified and willing.
If not, document good cause (§565.9(e)).
Offer choice of roommate and of staff where feasible.

policies.title: Referral, Admission and Transition In
state_specifics: Individuals reach the provider through the LIDDA choice list and the interest list (§263.103).
Written residential agreement before selection of the home.
Confirm home fit: 3-person (SL or RSS) or 4-person (RSS required for at least one resident when four live there).
Complete the transition with the LIDDA service coordinator, including the PDP and IPC.

policies.title: Person-Centered Planning and the Implementation Plan
state_specifics: The PDP and IPC are developed with the LIDDA service coordinator. The provider writes the implementation plan.
Staff who help develop an implementation plan for CFC PAS/HAB complete the HHSC Online Introductory Course to Person Centered Planning within 90 days of hire (§565.7(b)(2)(C)).
The RN writes the nursing portion of the implementation plan.

policies.title: Implementation of Supports and Daily Documentation
state_specifics: Staff are trained on each individual's needs before serving, and at least every 12 months, with observed competency.
Document service delivery contemporaneously. Only documented services support billing.
Services follow the implementation plan and IPC.

policies.title: Community Integration and Employment Choice
state_specifics: Support access to the community, to work, and to control personal resources.
Coordinate with day habilitation, individualized skills and socialization, and employment services.
Document the individual's choices and any assessed need to modify a right.

policies.title: Transition, Discharge, Transfer and Termination of Services
state_specifics: Transfers to another provider follow §263.701. Cooperate with the LIDDA and receiving provider.
Hand over records, medications and funds within the time the transfer process requires.
Document the individual's choice and the reason for any provider-initiated discharge, in coordination with the LIDDA.

policies.title: Coordination with the LIDDA Service Coordinator
state_specifics: Notify the service coordinator of changes in condition, refused nursing assessments and requested rights modifications.
Participate in PDP meetings and annual IPC renewals.
Keep contact information current for each LIDDA served.

policies.title: Medication Administration, Storage and Staff Delegation
state_specifics: Unlicensed staff give oral, topical or metered-dose inhaler medications for stable, predictable conditions only after RN assessment and RN/LVN training or competency check (Hum. Res. Code Ch. 161).
The RN/LVN reviews at least annually and after a significant change.
Written policy preventing unauthorized access to medications, with a safe administration procedure (§565.23(h)).
Accurate administration records, accessible to staff.

policies.title: Nursing Oversight and Health Care Coordination
state_specifics: The RN performs and documents a nursing assessment before unlicensed staff perform any nursing task, and when needs change (§565.13(a)(2)(J)).
The RN documents delegation decisions and develops the nursing portion of the implementation plan.
Nursing follows the Nursing Practice Act and 22 TAC Ch. 217, 224, 225.
Use the Nursing Task Screening Tool. Handle refusal of assessment per IR-07.

policies.title: Qualified Nursing, Dental and Therapy Providers
state_specifics: Only licensed providers in good standing, acting within the scope of their license, serve individuals (§565.7(c)).
Behavioral support providers take the HHSC web training before service, within 90 days of revision, and every 3 years.
Verify licenses at hire and periodically.

policies.title: Health Monitoring, Seizures and Choking Risk
state_specifics: Health monitoring is part of the RN's nursing scope. The RN builds seizure and choking-risk protocols into the implementation plan.
Staff are trained on each individual's protocols before serving them.
Keep adaptive equipment functional, or document why not (§565.23(b)).

policies.title: Change of Condition and Emergency Medical Care
state_specifics: Call 911 for emergencies, then notify the RN, program manager, LAR and service coordinator.
The RN reassesses after any health change before unlicensed staff continue nursing tasks.
Post emergency numbers where staff can see them (§565.23(f)).
Send medication lists and the face sheet with the individual to the hospital. No billing during inpatient stays.

policies.title: Death of an Individual
state_specifics: Notify emergency services, the LAR/family, service coordinator and HHSC promptly. Confirm required timeframes and reporting channels with HHSC before finalizing.
Preserve the scene and records. Cooperate with any investigation.
Hold a mortality review (GOV-04).
Secure personal funds and property per IR-05.

policies.title: Positive Behavior Support
state_specifics: Behavioral support providers take the HHSC web training (§565.7(c)).
Use proactive, individualized strategies. Document in the implementation plan.
Review data on behavior regularly.

policies.title: Restrictive Interventions, Restraint and Seclusion
state_specifics: Any restriction of a right must be in the PDP, based on an assessed need (§263.502(c)-(e)).
Use only HHSC-permitted interventions. Pull the exact Ch. 565 restraint text before drafting.
Restraint and seclusion are last-resort measures. Record and review every use.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Written policy preventing abuse, neglect and exploitation (§565.9(g)).
Staff are mandatory reporters. Report to the Texas Abuse Hotline (DFPS), 1-800-252-5400. Confirm the number and reporting rules against 40 TAC Ch. 49 before publication.
Screen staff through the Employee Misconduct Registry, Nurse Aide Registry and exclusion lists.
Protect the individual immediately, with no retaliation against reporters.

policies.title: Reportable Incidents and Investigations
state_specifics: Define reportable incidents and who is notified, and when. Confirm timeframes against current Ch. 565 and HHSC guidance.
Cooperate with HHSC and DFPS investigators.
Conduct an internal review and corrective action for each incident, and feed results into GOV-04.

policies.title: Missing Person and Elopement
state_specifics: Individualized elopement-risk plan in each emergency plan.
Search immediately, call 911 if the individual is not found, then notify the LAR, program manager and service coordinator.
Document the event and review the plan afterwards.

policies.title: Residential Environment and Accessibility
state_specifics: Home is clean and pest-free, with working appliances and HVAC.
Mattresses off the floor. Chemicals secured. Perishables stored safely. Pets vaccinated.
Bedroom locks at no cost to the individual.
Accessible and hazard-free for each resident.

policies.title: Hot Water Temperature and Skills Assessment
state_specifics: Hot water at sinks and bathing facilities must not exceed 120°F.
The exception requires a face-to-face competency-based skills assessment showing every resident can regulate temperature.
Repeat annually, document it, and keep a copy in the residence.

policies.title: Fire Safety, Means of Escape and Fire Drills
state_specifics: Two means of escape from the home and from each bedroom (one if sprinklered and maintained). Exterior doors unobstructed.
Working smoke alarms in and outside bedrooms. Extinguishers on each level, serviced after use.
Per residence: a drill at least every 90 days, four per 365 days, two during sleeping hours.
Each staff member drills within 90 days of hire and annually. Retrain and revise plans as needed.

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Individual Emergency Plans
state_specifics: Staff review each resident's emergency plans before serving.
Each home keeps plans for location-relevant emergencies (e.g., hurricane, flood, winter storm, tornado), individual needs and fire-drill responses.
Post emergency numbers where staff can see them.
Evacuation and shelter-in-place plans account for medications, equipment and communication needs.

policies.title: Four-Person Residence Approval and Annual Fire Inspection
state_specifics: Before RSS: local or State Fire Marshal inspection, correct cited items, then HHSC approval (§565.23(i), §565.43).
The request includes address/county, RSS-intent certification, fire-safety certification and occupancy certification. HHSC responds within 14 calendar days.
Renew fire certification annually, keep the latest inspection in the home, and stay in continuous compliance.
Forms 5604/5606 apply only if inspectors refuse.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Use standard precautions and hand hygiene (§565.23(g)).
Written policies preventing and controlling communicable disease among employees and individuals, including transmission-based precautions.
Protective measures when an employee contracts a communicable disease.
Offer bloodborne pathogen training and PPE per OSHA.

policies.title: Food, Nutrition and Modified Diets
state_specifics: Individuals have access to food at any time (§263.502).
Perishables stored safely (§565.23(b)).
Board charge covers food and cooking supplies only (§565.27).
RN or dietitian input for modified diets and choking-risk plans.

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
state_specifics: Only staff and service providers with a valid driver's license and insurance transport individuals (§565.9(c)).
Verify licenses and insurance at hire and annually.
Revise the policy when a shortcoming is identified.
Use seat belts and the equipment each individual needs.

policies.title: Staffing Coverage and Supervision (No Numeric Ratio)
state_specifics: Texas sets no numeric staff-to-resident ratio for SL or RSS.
RSS: staff present and awake whenever an individual is present. SL: staff present and able to respond during sleeping hours.
LON 9: dedicated staff at least 16 waking hours a day.
Schedule from each person's IPC and LON. Ensure continuous availability of trained staff (§565.9(a)).
Pay overtime per FLSA. HHSC rates assume a $13.00 average attendant wage.

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: DPS criminal history before hire. Do not hire anyone with a Health & Safety Code §250.006 offense, a registered sex offender, or an offense the provider deems a contraindication.
Employee Misconduct Registry and Nurse Aide Registry: before hire and every 12 months.
HHS-OIG and HHSC-OIG exclusion lists: before hire and monthly.
Do not employ listed persons.

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Orientation and Training
state_specifics: Individual-specific training before service and at least every 12 months, with observed competency (§565.7(b)).
Person-Centered Planning online course within 90 days where required (§565.7(b)(2)(C)).
Fire drill participation within 90 days of hire (§565.23(e)).
Medication staff are trained and delegated by the RN. Behavioral support providers take HHSC web training.

policies.title: Employee Health and Communicable Disease Screening
state_specifics: Written policy on protective measures when an employee contracts a communicable disease (§565.23(g)).
Confirm TB screening requirements with HHSC before finalizing. No specific TB rule was fact-checked.
Offer hepatitis B vaccination under OSHA.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Keep DPS results, registry and exclusion-search dates, training and competency records, and license/insurance verification.
Keep records of individual-specific training before service and every 12 months.
Keep I-9 and wage records per federal law.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: No exchange of goods or services between staff and individuals, apart from room and board (§565.9(g)).
No misuse of an individual's funds or property.
No damaging, or blocking access to, an individual's possessions, and no threats of these.
Violations lead to discipline and may require reporting under BP-03.

policies.title: Direct Service Provider Qualifications and Hiring
state_specifics: SL/RSS staff must meet HCS Billing Requirements and waiver Appendix C criteria (§565.7(b)).
CFC PAS/HAB providers: at least 18, with a diploma or documented proficiency evaluation with 3 references. Not the individual's spouse or a minor's parent (§565.7(e)).
The individual or LAR may train the provider on request.
Honor the individual's choice of provider where qualified and willing.

policies.title: Individual Records and Retention
state_specifics: Keep PDP, IPC, ID/RC assessment, LOC determination, implementation plan, RN assessments, daily documentation, and fund and property records.
Keep the hot-water skills assessment and emergency plans in the home.
Retention period: confirm the HHSC contract schedule. HIPAA documentation is retained 6 years.
Make records available to HHSC surveyors.

policies.title: Required Reports and Notices to HHSC
state_specifics: Written notice to HHSC when an individual or LAR refuses a nursing assessment (§565.13).
Four-person residence approval request and annual fire certification (§565.23(i), §565.43).
Respond to survey findings with amelioration plans.
Act on GovDelivery information letters and alerts.

policies.title: TMHP Portal, IPC Submissions and Cost Reporting
state_specifics: Submit IPCs and revisions through the TMHP LTC Online Portal.
Register in STEPS and file cost reports.
Keep the ID/RC assessment current before it expires (§263.106).
Reconcile claims against authorized IPCs monthly.

official.notes: No single official policy-review checklist for the Texas HCS residential program (Supervised Living / Residential Support Services in three- and four-person residences) is identified in the supplied research, and I did not use tools to open any document. Because the item text and numbering could not be confirmed from a source, I have not listed any required policy items; doing so would risk inventing them. Next steps: (1) open the CAPM 'How to Apply' PDF and the CAMP provisional-contract application materials to see whether they contain a policy or plan-of-operation checklist; (2) if they do not, extract the 'program provider must have written policies and procedures' provisions from 26 TAC Ch. 565 (starting with §565.7/§565.9, then §565.13, §565.23, §565.27) and from 26 TAC Ch. 263 (§263.502), keeping each provision's own subsection numbering (for example 'A(7)' or 'B9') as the item_id and cite; (3) for a four-person residence, add the §565.41/§565.43 approval requirements and the fire marshal inspection. Expected submission: electronically through the HHSC CAMP portal for the provisional contract, followed by the Pre-Award Training (PAT) exam request and a later LTCR certification survey. Organization of the manual should follow the Ch. 565 section order once the items are extracted, since there is no verified checklist section order to mirror.
